title: provider.watch() runs on the main thread and calls realpath(), so a dead share freezes launch or navigation.
detail: updateWatchers() calls provider.watch(directories) synchronously. LocalFileSystem.watch goes to DirectoryWatcher.watch -> resolve -> realpath() for every directory. watch is not on the provider contract list of main-thread-safe calls. Scenarios: last session ended on /Volumes/share/x and the share is dead, PanelCoordinator.init calls updateWatchers() before anything is read so launch blocks in realpath with no window; right panel on a share that stalls later, any navigation in the left local panel re-resolves both directories and the app freezes; switching to a restored tab on a dead share posts panelDidChangeLocation at once (line 409) before its read. The comment at PanelViewController.swift:735-737 shows the hazard is known; only one path was deferred.
fix: Create and replace watchers off the main thread on a serial queue with a generation check when installing. Watch only directories whose listing just succeeded. Do not re-resolve a panel directory that did not change.

title: Read-ahead loops forever on a remote folder with more than 300,000 entries.
detail: ListingCache.store refuses a listing above maxEntries and returns false. ended() re-arms the dwell whenever resting != nil. dwellEnded() only checks cache.age (nil here) and failures (not a failure), so it starts the read again. Scenario: cursor rests on a 1M-entry folder of a share; the whole folder is listed, 1M FileItems allocated and sorted on all cores, the result thrown away, and 0.4 s later it starts again for as long as the cursor stays. Contradicts the class comment "One listing per rest of the cursor". Category: performance/network.
fix: Record per location in ReadAhead when it was last read ahead whatever the cache did, and honour freshEnough against that. Or do not re-dwell in ended() for the target just read. Ideally stop the read once it exceeds maxEntries.

title: NSWorkspace.icon(forFile:) runs on the main thread for every newly drawn row and can stall on slow or remote files.
detail: Reported as MEDIUM-HIGH, freeze. The call touches the file and is gated only by model.volume?.isLocal, which describes the directory, not the items. VirtualFileSystem.volume returns isLocal: entries.allSatisfy(\.isFileURL), so a search result holding files on /Volumes/<share> gets one server round trip per row in viewFor/draw; a stalled share hangs the main thread while scrolling. Same for symlinks in a local folder pointing to a share, a spun-down external disk, File Provider/iCloud items, disk images hosted on a share. ArchiveFileSystem builds VolumeInfo(name:) with default isLocal: true. The cache is cleared whole at 4000 entries (line 119): not steady-state thrash, but every 4000 new rows the visible rows of both panels miss again on main. Confirmed that the call is on main and the virtual-folder path reaches it; the stall itself is plausible.
fix: Never ask for a file own icon on the main thread. Return the type icon at once, fetch own icons on a small background queue keyed by path+date, cancel on scroll, redraw the row on arrival (ThumbnailStore pattern). Use LRU instead of clear-all. Decide per item (item volume or mount point), not per directory.

title: A job that never returns blocks all commands forever and Quit hangs.
detail: applicationShouldTerminate returns .terminateLater and replies only when the queue is empty. isBusy (and so commands.isBlocked) stays true until work returns; no timeout and no abandon. Scenario: a copy to a stalled NFS/SMB mount sits in a kernel write; Cancel shows "Stopping..." indefinitely and every file or panel command stays rejected; Cmd+Q puts the app in the terminate-later modal loop with no way back, user must force-quit. Depends on a provider that cannot abort. Category: freeze.
fix: After N seconds of "Stopping..." offer "Quit anyway" or "Abandon job". On quit use cancelAll with a deadline, then reply(true).

title: Every successful reload of the active tab posts .locationChanged, which closes Quick View and does extra work on every watcher tick.
detail: if tab === self.model { host?.panelDidChangeLocation(self) } runs after quiet reloads too (app activation, watcher events, the refresh after each job). QuickViewPanel dismisses itself on .locationChanged of the covered panel. Scenario: Quick View open; switching to another app and back, or any other program touching the covered folder, closes it. Side effects: prompt update, Places tracker and bar validation also run on every watcher tick. Category: correctness.
fix: Keep the last location announced per panel and post only when it differs. That also fixes finding 11.

title: In-place rename is cancelled by any redraw and the panel loses keyboard focus.
detail: redraw() calls cancelRename(): every .contents change of the active tab cancels the edit and discards typed text. Sources: setVolume after volumeInfoDidChange (any listing on the same volume, e.g. the other panel watcher reload), a piece arriving, fresh listing replacing a remembered one, settings changes. Rename is enabled while the tab is still loading or refreshing, so "enter a remembered share folder, start renaming, fresh listing lands a second later" is routine. cancelRename removes the field without makeFirstResponder(listView); experiment fr.swift shows the window itself becomes first responder, so keys beep until the user clicks. Category: correctness.
fix: Do not cancel for changes that keep the row (volume, flags); re-anchor the editor by item name after a reload. When cancelling programmatically restore the first responder if the field had it. (Responder part confirmed by experiment, rest by reading.)

title: A joined read-ahead cannot be cancelled and a retry re-joins the same stalled read.
detail: The panel Load.flag is not connected to reading.cancellation. After join the reading runs to its end even if the panel moves on. Scenario: read-ahead of folder F starts and the server stalls; Enter joins it and shows "Reading F..."; user navigates away and back; join matches the same uncancelled read again. A normal load cancel would have let the provider close the hung connection and reconnect. Side effect: reading != nil also disables all further read-ahead for the session. Category: threading/stuck loading.
fix: When the last waiter is superseded cancel the reading (chain via flag.onCancel). Do not join a reading older than a few seconds. (Confidence: plausible.)

title: Modal dialogs are started from inside main-queue blocks, where a nested run loop does not drain the main queue.
detail: Experiment nested.swift shows a nested run loop inside DispatchQueue.main.async does not run other main-queue blocks, while one started from a run-loop callback does. Affected: "The folder cannot be read!" alert (PanelViewController 682-684); PanelViewController+Interaction 323 -> carryOut (confirmation, then plugin copy dialogs); every job completion (ProgressJobService 78-86); ask via main.sync (223); every Load.complete (plugin completions of show/reload). Consequences: while such an alert is up nothing dispatched to main runs (other panel pieces, watcher events, progress renders, every asyncAfter timer, ask from a background-mode job); startNext() waits for the dialog so the next queued job does not start; anything a plugin opens from these callbacks relying on main-queue delivery while modal hangs, e.g. NSApp.runModal(for:) windows with asynchronously filled content (CommandBrowser, HotlistEditor) or NSApp.terminate -> .terminateLater whose reply arrives via main.async; same command behaves differently from menu/key than from a drop or completion. Mechanism confirmed; plugin-side hang plausible.
fix: Leave the main queue before going modal, e.g. RunLoop.main.perform(inModes: [.common]) or CFRunLoopPerformBlock + CFRunLoopWakeUp, for report, carryOut, job completions and Load.complete. Or use sheets and non-modal alerts.

title: A stale background quick-filter result falls back to filtering the whole list on the main thread.
detail: tab.setFilter(filter, prefiltered:listVersion:) with a stale version makes the model filter listedItems itself on main. listVersion moves with every arriving piece, every computed folder size and every reload. Scenario: typing a quick filter in a 1M folder still arriving makes every result stale, O(n) matches pass on main per key burst. Also the kernel setListed re-filters the full list on main for every piece while a filter is set. Also: narrowing is ignored on the background path. Category: performance/freeze.
fix: On a version mismatch re-run the job in the background against the new list, never on main. Filter incoming pieces in the loader thread.

title: No back-off between quiet re-reads: continuous writes in a large folder cause back-to-back full reads and sorts.
detail: FSEvents deliver about 2 events/s per stream. A read longer than that marks the tab dirty and rereadIfDirty starts the next read immediately. Scenario: another program writes continuously into a shown 1M-entry folder; the app reads and sorts it on all cores back to back indefinitely, each round ending in an O(n) tab.update and full redraw() on main. Related: after each job the plugin refresh (not quiet) is followed by jobsEnded (quiet -> dirty -> second full read). Category: performance.
fix: Enforce a minimum gap e.g. max(1 s, 2 x last read time) with one trailing coalesced reread. Skip the jobsEnded reread for directories just refreshed.

title: A location change is never announced when a load of the same location overtakes one that already opened it.
detail: Reported MEDIUM-LOW. previousDirectory is tab.directory at load start, which is already B once the 0.1 s timer has opened B. Scenario: click a drive button for a slow share; after "Reading..." click it again or press Ctrl+R. The second load ends with B == B so no panelDidChangeLocation is posted. Watchers stay on A, the command-line prompt shows A, Places is not told. Category: correctness.
fix: As in finding 5 (keep last announced location per panel and post only when it differs).

title: Drag and drop is O(s) on the main thread with heavy constants (drag start, hover, drop).
detail: Reported MEDIUM-LOW, performance. Drag start: operands() is O(n), then one NSPasteboardItem (grid also one NSDraggingItem) per marked item. Measured in bench.swift: 0.30 s for creating 100k pasteboard items alone before writeObjects; with 1M marked several seconds and gigabytes. Hover: isPointless is cached per destination but each newly hovered folder row costs O(s) locationKey constructions (two or three per source), roughly 0.5-1 s for 100k sources. Drop side: pasteboardItems is O(s) again per panel entered.
fix: Use a single pasteboard item with a lazy provider, or cap the items and carry the rest in-process. Precompute once per drag the set of source parent keys and source keys; the check becomes O(depth) per destination. (Measured for creation; rest by reading.)

title: Type-to-select is O(n) per keystroke on the main thread.
detail: Reported LOW-MEDIUM, performance. In the Full view NSTableView own type-select calls typeSelectStringFor for every row. Measured 221 ms per key for 1M names when nothing matches.
fix: Names are sorted, so binary search when sorted by name. Otherwise search in the background with a generation, or cap the work per key.

title: ColumnValueStore stops for good after one stalled value.
detail: Reported LOW-MEDIUM, threading/stuck. One batch at a time. A column.value call blocked on a dead share leaves isWorking true; reset() does not clear it and there is no cancellation. Effect: plugin columns stay empty in every folder of that panel for the rest of the session.
fix: Tie isWorking to the generation so a reset frees it, bound abandoned batches, give ContentColumn.value a cancellation flag.

title: Blocking file-system work runs on DispatchQueue.global, so stalled shares can exhaust the constrained thread pool.
detail: Reported LOW-MEDIUM, threading. Every retry on a stalled share parks another pool thread; each Space on a folder (:954) does too, and ParallelPool adds more. Effect: once the constrained pool is exhausted every panel read in every tab stops and a newly started job work never begins while isBusy stays true. The exact pool limit was not measured. Confidence plausible.
fix: Use dedicated bounded queues or threads per provider or volume for blocking I/O.

title: Drop type afm.panel-item is accepted from any application and turned into URLs of any scheme.
detail: Security. Accepts afm.panel-item from any app and turns it into URLs of any scheme; the drop kind (move vs copy) is derived from it. A foreign drag can name sftp://..., archive or arbitrary local sources that plugins will then open or move.
fix: Accept this type only when info.draggingSource is one of our own views, and verify that the scheme has a provider.

title: Untrusted file names are shown raw (newlines, bidi controls) in path bar, cells, tab titles, tooltips, alerts and progress lines.
detail: Names do not neutralise newlines or bidi controls (U+202E etc.). A name can display with a spoofed extension, or hide its second line in the 20 pt row. Security, low.
fix: Map control and bidi-override characters to visible placeholders for display.

title: File promises are not accepted on drop (not a defect).
detail: Noted in the security finding as not a defect.

title: ProgressSheet.lastReport is unsynchronised and could race if a plugin reports from parallel workers.
detail: Safe today only because callers serialise their reports (FileJob under its counters lock; Unpacker and Sync callers report from the job thread). A plugin reporting from parallel workers would race. Plausible.
fix: Use a lock or an atomic.

title: Out-of-order progress reports can make latest step backwards.
detail: Out-of-order reports can make ProgressSheet latest step backwards.

title: ask deadlocks or traps if called on the main thread.
detail: ask uses DispatchQueue.main.sync without the Thread.isMainThread guard that Kernel.askUser has.
fix: Add the Thread.isMainThread guard as Kernel.askUser has.

title: Pause holds the caller locks: PauseGate blocks inside report(), so a paused worker keeps its caller locks and could deadlock the UI.
detail: PauseGate blocks inside report(), so a paused worker keeps whatever lock its caller holds. FileJob calls report under counters, so sibling workers queue on that lock. If any main-thread code (e.g. an ask question closure) took that lock while paused, the UI would deadlock with Resume unreachable. Plausible; FileJob ask closures were not checked.
fix: Pause at a point where the caller holds nothing, or document the constraint.

title: QueuedJob.start is never cleared after it ran, so a plugin keeping the JobHandle keeps work and completion captures alive.
detail: QueuedJob.start never cleared after running.

title: A read cancelled because the cursor moved on is recorded as a failure when the provider throws on cancellation, blocking read-ahead for that folder for 60 s.
detail: Coming back to that folder gets no read-ahead for 60 s. Plausible.

title: ReadAhead failures dictionary is never pruned.
detail: failures is never pruned.

title: The 100 ms validation tick runs arbitrary plugin enabled:/checked: closures that can be O(n) or do IPC.
detail: Tick is triggered by NSWindow.didUpdateNotification i.e. after every event. Default bar is O(1). Costly closures once the user puts them on the bar or holds the modifier showing them on the F-key bar: Print `!localFiles().isEmpty` -> operands().filter is O(n) with marks; Paste pasteboard.canReadObject(...) is IPC and may wait on a lazy provider; Paste Path availableType. Category: performance.
fix: Require enabled to be O(1) and free of I/O, or memoise per panel-event generation.

title: A non-quiet reload cancels a pending navigation and re-reads the old folder.
detail: refresh or Ctrl+R within the first 100 ms of a navigation supersedes it and re-reads the old folder. Category: correctness, load state machine.

title: A failed non-quiet reload is silent and a partial list is marked complete.
detail: try? swallows the error and a partial list is marked complete by finishLoading().

title: Load completions are never called for loads of a closed tab and after cancelLoading().
detail: Completions never called for loads of a closed tab and after cancelLoading().

title: A quiet reload that is turned away calls completion at once, before any read.
detail: Completion called too early.

title: Phantom history: a folder opened at 0.1 s then superseded stays in history, so Back leads to a place never shown.
detail: Recorded with .record.

title: Empty flash: the 0.1 s timer and the loader first piece race, so a folder taking just over 100 ms flashes empty with "Reading..." before its first piece.
detail: Loader first piece also about 0.1 s; the same happens while a first/last piece is held for a background re-sort.

title: Rare main-thread sort: if the order changes a second time during the background re-sort, the model sorts the full list on main.
detail: In sorted() or after cache.entry(sortedBy:).

title: places() can wait up to 1 s on the main thread at launch.
detail: Bounded freeze. DriveBarView.rebuild from the window init: the first call can hit LocalFileSystem.places() placesCondition.wait(until: +1 s) when the first volume scan is slow.

title: dropSession is not cleared when a drag leaves the table, retaining the source array until the next drag.
detail: Only the grid clears it.

title: FileListColumn.typeIcons is unbounded by distinct extensions.
detail: Leaks/unbounded state.

title: missedChanges accumulates duplicates for the length of a job.
detail: Unbounded state.

title: Closures of in-flight loads capture PanelViewController and PanelModel strongly on background threads; last release could happen off main.
detail: Only at teardown.

title: Main-thread cost per event table (n entries, v visible rows, s marked, t tabs).
detail: Cursor key repeat O(1) plus subscribers with one asyncAfter per move; insert/toggle O(v) redraw; select all/invert O(n) once; shift+click O(range); mouse move O(path depth); scroll table O(v x columns) with one icon(forFile:) per new row (finding 3); thumbnails scroll O(v); live resize O(v); arriving piece/any .contents change redraw(): O(v) reloadData + O(depth) path bar + O(t) tab bar + O(n) totals recount plus kernel O(n) cursor lookup and O(n) filtering with a filter; quiet reload result O(n) update(with:) diff, free space almost always differs; watcher event O(1) then full background read (finding 10); progress report O(1) throttled 20/s; validation tick O(buttons x closure) (finding 19); drag update O(1) known destination, O(s) new (finding 12); drag start O(n+s); type-select O(n) worst case (finding 13); quick-filter keystroke debounced 0.1 s, under 20k entries O(n) on main, larger in background except finding 9.

title: Shared state touched off the main thread is protected.
detail: Load.flag, Reading.cancellation, size-calculation flags: CancellationFlag (NSLock). PanelLoading.OrderBox: NSLock. ListingCache: one NSLock not held while sorting. PanelLoading.start locals owned by one background closure, pieces immutable. ReadAhead: all state on main, background touches only flag and cache. ColumnValueStore, ThumbnailStore: main only, batches copy what they need, QuickLook completions hop to main and are token-checked. Load closure state main only. PauseGate: NSCondition. ProgressSheet.latest and rate: main only. FileListColumn icon caches main only. getmntinfo static buffer used only from main and nowhere else. Exception: ProgressSheet.lastReport unprotected (finding 17).

title: Superseding is correct: every piece, end and timer callback is guarded by loads[id] === load; completions fire at most once.
detail: Load.complete fires at most once. A superseded load completion(false) arrives after its successor is installed.

title: Piece ordering is correct: pieces and end are FIFO on main; the inOrder/isHolding hold is correct including a second order change during the re-sort.
Retries cannot loop: the one-shot automatic retry always takes the listed-reload path; loadRestored and loadInitially terminate at the root.
Tab bookkeeping is sound: openedFrom snapshots, the dirty set and per-tab dictionaries are pruned in tabsChanged; identifier reuse is harmless.
detail: Weak tabs, generation counters.

title: Stream contract: PanelLoader.stream always delivers at least one batch unless cancelled, so .success(nil) cannot strand a current load.
Table safety: row count and viewFor cannot disagree in a crashing way; model changes reload synchronously on main; item(atRow:) is bounds-checked.

Job queue is sound: FIFO order holds, chained completions work, cancelAll does not wait synchronously, main never blocks on a job, no ask-versus-quit deadlock on normal quit paths (menu, button, AppleEvent), jobsEnded replays missed watcher events correctly.
Observers are added once; volume observer removed in deinit; volumeInfoDidChange cannot sustain itself; the validation tick has no feedback loop.
detail: The provider measures at most once per age window.

title: Tab drag loop exits safely if the strip is rebuilt under it.
Quick filter debounce, generation and binding to the tab are correct.
Parallel.map on main is safe: the caller waits only for pieces of its own CPU-only job, so stalled workers elsewhere in the pool cannot block it.
Nothing was run against the real app, a real stalled mount or with TSan.
detail: Stall findings rest on documented syscall behaviour plus code reading.

title: Plugin internals read only where the shell calls into them; FileJob ask closures not checked for lock use, nor plugin completions for modal windows depending on main-queue delivery.
Not measured: whether NSPasteboard.canReadObject blocks on lazy data, nor the exact GCD pool limit on this OS version.
Tests/ was not read.
Replacing move deletes the destination when the rename is refused for any reason (data loss).
detail: move(replacing: true) treats every NetworkError.refused as "something is in the way", removes the destination, then renames again. The SFTP fallback maps every SFTPError (permission denied, no such file) to a 550. Scenario: an FTP account that may delete but not rename (RNFR/RNTO answers 550/502), or an SFTP server without posix-rename. FileJob extend writes a temporary file then calls move(temporary, to: destination, replacing: true); rename refused, destination deleted, second rename fails, FileJob catch discards the temporary. Both old and new file are gone. Same when the second rename fails transiently after the remove.
fix: Move the existing destination aside under a backup name, rename the new file in, then delete the backup; restore on failure. Only take this path when the server answer plausibly means "exists". Do not turn every SFTP error into 550.

title: LIST parser regexes are quadratic on long lines and line length is unbounded (security/freeze).
detail: Unanchored (\d+)\s+... patterns backtrack quadratically. A line "-rwxrwxrwx " followed by N digits took 3.2 s at 8 KB, 13.6 s at 16 KB and 66 s at 32 KB for one of the three regexes. A hostile server or MITM on plain FTP sends a few such lines; the listing thread spins for hours and cannot be cancelled. A batch of 2000+ lines goes through Parallel.map and occupies every core of the shared pool. Related: rest grows without limit when no LF arrives and is re-split on every block.
fix: Reject lines over about 4 KB before parsing, cap rest, anchor or pre-tokenise the patterns.

title: FTP replies are unbounded (security/freeze).
detail: A multi-line reply (220- followed by endless lines) accumulates forever; timeout is per line and one line may be about 1.25 MB. abortTransfer and isAlive from the keep-alive read with cancellation: nil, so that thread never returns and memory grows.
fix: Cap lines per reply (about 1000), bytes per reply (about 64 KB), line length (about 4 KB), use one deadline per reply.

title: Active mode can return a desynchronised connection to the pool (correctness/data loss).
detail: After the 1xx reply a cancel or timeout in listener.accept throws without setting isBroken and without reading the final reply. release sees isUsable and pools the connection. The next command reads the stale 425/426 and the one after reads its predecessor reply. An MLST that reads a foreign 250 returns nil ("does not exist"), so the following STOR overwrites without asking.
fix: Once the command got a 1xx, any failure before setStreams must set isBroken unless the final reply was read. (Plausible.)

title: Active-mode listener accepts the first connection from anyone (security).
detail: Listener is on all interfaces and the peer is never compared with the control connection remote address. A LAN host that connects first receives the upload, or supplies the download or listing.
fix: Check the accepted peer against control.remoteAddress, reject others and keep waiting; bind to the control connection local address.

title: Waits that are not cancellable and have no time limit (threading/freeze).
detail: While the first FTP login waits for the user at a password or certificate dialog, every other thread using that session blocks in loginLock.lock() (113) with no way out. makeDirectory, remove, rename and setAttributes pass no cancellation in either protocol so they loop indefinitely in acquire (202-232) or on connectLock (SFTP 84-86). A reader waiting for a transfer slot also has no deadline: with four paused viewers on one server a fifth read or a copy hangs silently.
fix: Use lock(before:) in a loop with cancellation as SFTP already does; give slot and pool waits a deadline and clear error; pass a cancellation flag through the four mutating calls.

title: Background link resolution holds a pooled command connection for up to 20 s and is unbounded in number.
detail: Every listing with unresolved links queues a block that takes a command connection, with no cancellation and no yielding to waiting user commands. With parallelConnections at 1, or three link-heavy folders, navigation stalls 20 s or more. Rapid browsing piles blocks up in acquire, each a blocked GCD thread, for folders the user has left. Side effect: each resolved link calls cache.update; once the listing is older than 10 s this forgets the directory and journals "unknown", so listings in flight are not stored and a copy job re-lists.
fix: One resolver per session, release the connection between probes when anyone waits, drop work for folders no longer shown, make the observer a no-op when the entry is not cached.

title: Background.queue can exhaust the process-wide GCD thread pool.
detail: Every cancelled or dropped reader or writer queues a block that waits for a server (closeHandle up to timeout, abortTransfer 10 s or more) on a concurrent queue. A stalled server plus Quick View stepping through files or many cancelled transfers produces dozens of blocked workers. At 64, every DispatchQueue.global() user in the app starves. Plausible.
fix: Small fixed worker pool or a serial queue per session. For SFTP send CLOSE synchronously (a pipe write) and never wait for its answer.

title: An SFTP channel is never declared dead after timeouts.
detail: A timeout abandons one request only. With keep-alive set to 0, or on a black-holed path, ssh does not exit. Every later request waits the full timeout again: 1000-file delete costs 1000 x 30 s, a listing with 100 links 100 x 30 s, each cleanup block 30 s. Plausible.
fix: Close the channel after a timeout during which nothing arrived from the server; always pass ServerAliveInterval.

title: SFTP CLOSE status is discarded, so close(attributes:) reports success when the server close fails (data loss).
detail: closeHandle uses try?, so deferred write errors such as quota or NFS, or a close timeout, are not reported.
fix: The writer should send CLOSE itself and throw on a bad status.

title: A mid-window SFTP write error can leave a hole that Resume accepts (data loss).
detail: Up to 63 later writes are already on the wire when one fails. If the server refuses one (ENOSPC, EIO) and accepts the rest, the partial file has a 32 KB zero gap up to 2 MB before its end. FileJob resumeInPlace compares only the last 1 MB unless Verify is on, so the gap can survive into the finished file. Plausible.
fix: On the first failed write truncate the handle to the failed offset (fsetstat size) before closing.

title: FTP upload length is checked only for REST+STOR (data loss).
detail: No SIZE check after APPE or plain STOR, and the check is silently skipped when SIZE gives no answer. A server implementing APPE as STOR leaves a "resumed" file containing only the tail with a 226. A truncated TLS upload that still gets a 226 is also undetected. Plausible.
fix: After every binary upload on a server with SIZE, compare with start + written.

title: Download-list lines can be injected through remote names (security).
detail: Lines are written as displayPath + " -> " + target with no escaping. Parsing splits on every isNewline character (LF, CR, U+2028, U+0085, VT) and isSafeName allows all of them and " -> ". Scenario: a server offers /pub/payload -> /Users/me/Library/LaunchAgents/x.plist<U+2028>sleep:1; if the user adds it to a list and runs it, /pub/payload is downloaded to that local path followed by a rename with replacing: true.
fix: Refuse or escape names containing newline characters or the separator when writing; treat list contents as untrusted when running.

title: One cancelled SFTP write can close the shared channel for everyone.
detail: A cancel arriving mid-packet gets 2 s, then the shared channel is closed. On a slow uplink the pipe is always full, so cancelling one upload kills every other transfer and the panels. Plausible.
fix: Let the packet finish (at most about 32 KB) under the normal write timeout.

title: Fixed 64-request SFTP window causes head-of-line blocking on slow links.
detail: Window is 2 MB whatever the line speed and every read tops it up afterwards. At 1 Mbit/s a listing queues 16 s behind each active transfer and times out at 30 s with two; a viewer that reads one page still pulls up to 2 MB. Plausible.
fix: Size the window from measured throughput (about 1-2 s of data) and top up only after a sequential continuation.

title: ServerKey.url falls back to file:/// and IDN hosts change key.
detail: URLComponents.url is nil for hosts containing % # ? " < ^ { |, a space or bidi characters, all of which ServerAddress accepts; the remote location silently becomes the local root. Also bucher.de (bücher.de) comes back as xn--bcher-kva.de; the announced profile and panel URL then have different keys, so a second session logs in anonymously and typed credentials are dropped.
fix: Validate hosts in ServerAddress and ServerKey (IDNA-normalise once) and return an optional or throw instead of a file URL.

title: A changed certificate is not distinguished from first use (security).
detail: When a host already has an accepted fingerprint and presents a different untrusted certificate, the same dialog appears with "Yes" as the only button. Other observation: exceptions are keyed by host without port; host A exception cannot be used for host B.
fix: A distinct, stronger warning showing old and new fingerprints.

title: "User declined" memory is also set by ordinary cancellation.
detail: The user leaves during a slow connect and retries within 5 s; the retry fails with "The operation was cancelled" without trying.
fix: Record declined only when a dialog was refused.

title: File names do not round-trip (encoding and normalisation).
detail: FTP automatic mode decodes non-UTF-8 names as CP1252 but always encodes UTF-8. Both protocols force NFC on send so NFD names on byte-comparing servers are not found. SFTP decodes invalid UTF-8 lossily. allowLossyConversion turns unencodable characters into ?, which can address a different file.
fix: Keep the raw bytes with the entry, or at least remember the encoding and normalisation used to decode; fail on lossy encodes.

title: The entry cache can answer "absent" wrongly before an overwriting STOR or rename (data loss).
detail: Lookups are case-sensitive and up to 10 s old. FTP STOR and posix-rename overwrite silently. On a case-insensitive server File.txt overwrites file.txt without a prompt; so does a file created elsewhere within the 10 s. Plausible.
fix: Before a destructive open or rename treat a cached "absent" as unknown and ask the server.

title: Close of a cancelled SFTP handle races with the following remove or rename.
detail: closeHandleLater runs on another queue so FileJob remove of the partial file can reach the server first. Servers with Windows semantics refuse it and leave the partial file; handles also leak when the close times out. Plausible.
fix: As in finding 8: send CLOSE in order and do not wait.

title: Up to about 11 logins per server.
detail: 3 command connections plus 4 readers plus 4 writers at the default setting. Servers with a per-IP limit answer 421; after 10.5 s of back-off the transfer fails.
fix: One shared cap, with transfers borrowing idle command connections.

title: Mount error message prints the URL including the password.
detail: The mount error prints url.absoluteString, password included.

title: A quick-connect password is saved to the Keychain even when the user unticked "Keep the password".
The password is stored before the login succeeded.
SavedConnections delete-then-add with ignored results loses the old password when the add fails.
removingPassword misses addresses without :// and passwords containing /.
detail: Applied only to lastServer; other modules that store typed text (command line, target history) were not checked.

title: ssh invocation: no option injection (host after --, user via -l checked for leading -, numeric port); nothing secret in argv, environment or files; FIFOs 0600 in a 0700 directory; stderr capped at 8 KB and never parsed for prompts.
ssh invocation lacks -o RemoteCommand=none, PermitLocalCommand=no, ControlMaster=no and -T; with ControlMaster auto, disconnecting can SIGTERM the user master and end terminal sessions.
Askpass uses the first @, so a user name containing @ never gets the stored password; a question without @ gets it unconditionally.
Server-supplied keyboard-interactive text reaches the dialog unmarked, so a server can show "Enter passphrase for key ..."; a prompt containing (yes/no is treated as a confirmation.
A wrong stored password is never re-asked; the saved connection fails until it is edited.
SSH_ASKPASS_PROMPT (FIDO touch notices) is ignored, and an answer written after the helper script died stays in the FIFO and answers the next question.
The last three stderr lines, including the server banner, are shown as the error text.
The 64 MB packet limit is allocated on a hostile length.
fix: 1 MB is ample.

title: SFTP link stats are waited one by one each with a full timeout; tickets leak in waiting when a send throws.
A server with a read limit below 32 KB costs serial follow-ups per chunk; a seek discards everything in flight and the next small read asks for 256 KB.
disconnect() does not stop a login in progress, and a channel opened afterwards is stored in the closed session.
A second 1xx is taken as the verdict and leaves the 226 unread.
A listing has no entry or byte cap.
currentProfile is read after unlock (data race).
atEnd is written by close() from another thread (FTPReader).
detail: atEnd and position unprotected against a cross-thread close().

title: location(from:) announces as a side effect and can drop a session that is in the middle of its login.
NetStream does one dispatch per line read.
Disconnect on the main thread is bounded at 2 s per idle FTP connection (QUIT) and 0.5 s per SFTP channel.
NetFSMountURLSync cannot be cancelled.
detail: It runs in a job, not on the main thread.

title: Shared state: SFTPChannel.waiting/nextID/closed/errorText under lock; pipe writes and fd close under writeLock; Pending uses NSCondition with predicate loop (no lost wake-up); SFTPSession fields under lock with logins serialised by connectLock (except disconnect during login); SFTP reader/writer single owner plus CancellationFlag; NetStream condition for all state, every wait has a timeout, buffer bounded at about 1.25 MB; FTPConnection single owner with streamsLock for interrupt; FTPSession pool counters under condition, balanced on every traced path; LinkMemory, EntryCache, CertificateTrust, NetworkOptions, ConnectionCenter each own lock, leaf locks except center -> session state lock with no reverse path; NetworkCommands, ConnectionStore, ListRun main thread only.
detail: No lock-order inversion found. Kernel.askUser uses main.sync while loginLock or connectLock is held; safe only because no main-thread path takes those locks, which holds today.

title: capabilities(for:), places(), displayPath, parent(of:) and canAppend take only short state locks, never one held during I/O.
TLS: verification uses a host or IP policy, minimum TLS 1.2, PROT P enforced, USER/PASS sent only after the handshake; a refused AUTH TLS is an error.
PASV/EPSV: address in the reply is ignored and the port range-checked; data connections go to the control connection peer.
Command injection: CR, LF and NUL are rejected in every FTP command.

Sliding-window bookkeeping handles out-of-order replies, short replies, EOF mid-window, late replies to abandoned ids and interrupt() giving up only its own ids; a failed write is sticky and close throws it.
NetStream send-piece ordering, the waiting state when the network is down (fails at once), and continuation patterns (no double resume) are correct.
421 back-off sleeps on the calling worker in 0.1 s slices and is cancellable.
Keychain items carry no host or user in their attributes; URLs never carry credentials.
The ssh child is reaped by Process.
No critical issue, and no way for the main thread to block on a server for more than about 2 s.
Whether bytes following the 234 in the same segment go to TLS or to the application after prependApplicationProtocol (STARTTLS injection) was not reviewed.
How Network.framework reports a TLS stream that ends without close_notify is unknown, so download truncation by an active attacker is unassessed.
Whether NWConnection.cancel() always flushes the last TLS records of an upload was not verified; the code relies on a test.
Callers outside the plugin not checked: where typed addresses with passwords are stored, and whether FileReader.close() (blocks up to timeout for SFTP) is ever called on the main thread.
Nothing was run against real servers; the project was not built and its tests were not run.
A file name can run commands through the default %N in every shell (grapheme-cluster escaping hole).
detail: ShellWords.escaped walks Characters (grapheme clusters). A ", backtick or \ followed by a combining mark or variation selector is one Character not equal to the bare ASCII char so it is not escaped. needsQuoting works on scalars so the value is still wrapped in "...", and the shell sees a raw quote or backtick. The single-quote branch has the same hole: replacingOccurrences(of: "'") does not match ' + U+0301 (harness printed an unescaped result). Trigger: file named backtick+U+0301 ;touch PWNED; backtick+U+0301 (or the double-quote variant) under the cursor, with any user command, button or Start-menu entry using %N, %S, %P%N, x%Ny, --out=%N, "%N", "pre %N post" or %|VAR|. touch PWNED ran in zsh, bash, sh, dash, ksh (and tcsh/csh without -l). The '%N' form fell to the name. Lesser effect: $ + U+0301 not escaped either; bash and ksh passed a mangled name (wrong file, no execution).
fix: Escape per Unicode scalar or UTF-8 byte, never per Character. Better, stop pasting values into shell text (see finding 2).

title: Quote tracking does not understand command substitution, backticks, $'...', comments, here-docs or \%N, allowing injection with ordinary names.
detail: The tracker only toggles on " and '. Confirmed injections (touch PWNED ran): template "$(printf %s %N)" name a;touch PWNED; in zsh, bash, sh, dash, ksh; "$(printf %s "%N")" (the correct way to write it) same five, line becomes ""a;touch PWNED;""; backtick printf %s %N with name $(touch PWNED) in bash, sh, dash, ksh (backtick layer strips the backslash; not zsh); $'%N' with name \';touch PWNED;# in zsh, bash, ksh (4 of 7 shells); "# %N" with a newline name in bash, sh, dash, ksh (not zsh); here-doc body with backtick+U+0301 name (finding-1 hole) in all seven; \%N with name a;touch PWNED;" in ksh.
fix: Do not interpolate. Export each value as an environment variable or positional parameter and substitute a reference ("$AFM_1"), run as sh -c "$line" afm "$@". If interpolation stays, refuse placeholders inside $(, backticks, $' and after backslash.

title: Settings import is silent, unrestricted, and can plant commands, key bindings and hotlist entries that run later.
detail: restore writes every key in the file, not only known ones; validate checks only the shape of four keys. No confirmation and no summary of what will run. An archive can set user commands, Start-menu entries and key bindings (e.g. Return or F5 bound to em_x whose command is a shell line), effective immediately via applyStoredSettings. It can set places.hotlist entries; HotlistAction runs any cm_/afm_/em_ command with a text argument, so an entry titled "Documents" with command afm_RunCommandLine curl ... | sh executes on click. It can set systemTools.terminal to any app path (launched on Open Terminal Here), plus whatever other plugins store (saved connections, editor/viewer commands: not verified, out of scope). afm_ImportSettings <path> accepts a .location argument so a hotlist entry or user command can import a file with no panel and no question.
fix: Whitelist keys; show a diff listing every command line, key binding, hotlist command and program path and require confirmation; never import from an argument without confirmation; restrict hotlist commands or show the command before running one from an import; cap file size (Data(contentsOf:) is unbounded).

title: $SHELL -l -c with POSIX-only quoting: csh/tcsh reject the flags and quoting is unsafe in other shells.
detail: tcsh and csh reject the flags ("Unknown option: -l", exit 1, confirmed): for a user whose shell is csh/tcsh every user command and every typed command line fails. If -l were dropped quoting is unsafe there: "a!b" gives "Event not found", and names with newline or backtick executed in the harness. fish and nu not tested; "...backtick..." is not POSIX-equivalent in fish and nu rejects \$. Category: correctness + security.
fix: Run user commands with a fixed /bin/zsh or /bin/sh (take PATH from the login shell once, off-main), or apply the finding-2 fix, which is shell-independent.

title: O(n) work on the main thread for virtual file lists (register, unique, watch, volume).
detail: register and unique compute locationKey and a [UInt8] copy per URL and scan every scheme under the registry lock. watch for a list resolves provider, parent and locationKey for every entry before taking the first 512. volume(of:) runs allSatisfy(\.isFileURL) over all entries. Trigger: feed a 1M-result search to the list box, or branch view of a huge selection: seconds of beach ball.
fix: Register the raw array and de-duplicate inside listing (already off-main); in watch stop after 512 distinct parents or precompute them off-main.

title: Tree scan and branch walk run at full priority with no I/O throttling into protected and cloud folders.
detail: Scan uses all cores at .userInitiated and keeps doing so up to 15 minutes after the window closes. No setiopolicy_np anywhere in the sources. A scan of / enters Desktop, Documents, Downloads, iCloud Drive, ~/Library/CloudStorage, Photos, Mail: a series of TCC prompts and materialisation of dataless File Provider directories, which can stall on the network. No SF_DATALESS check. No (device, inode) set in TreeScanner; cycles are prevented only because symlinks are skipped, which is sufficient. Category: performance.
fix: Scan on .utility with IOPOL_THROTTLE and fewer workers when hidden; skip dataless directories and known TCC roots unless the user expands them.

title: Tree quick search and expand-all run on the main thread.
detail: find visits up to count nodes per keystroke; the first pass also runs lowercased() for every node. Wildcard patterns call fnmatch with two String-to-C conversions per node and no failure memo; during a scan revision changes every link turn so the memo never holds. Option-Right or Option-click on a disclosure triangle falls through to NSOutlineView and expands everything, loading every row and starting one reading.async reader per unscanned folder. Category: freeze.
fix: Search off-main over a snapshot, or time-slice with a generation check; intercept recursive expand; cap concurrent on-demand readers.

title: The self-call guard misses mutual recursion across asynchronous steps (cm_wait loops forever).
detail: active is popped when perform returns, which happens before a cm_wait or a waited program continues. Trigger: em_a = "cm_wait 1, em_b" and em_b = "cm_wait 1, em_a" loop forever with no way to stop; with an external step it spawns processes endlessly. An imported settings file can contain this.
fix: Carry the call chain through the continuation instead of a stack; add a depth limit and a way to stop.

title: Each launched program pins a GCD thread; waiting chains cannot be cancelled.
detail: A worker thread blocks on a semaphore for the lifetime of every started process (.utility, or .userInitiated when a chain waits). A program that stays open in a chain (em_edit, cm_RereadSource) parks the chain indefinitely; main is not blocked but the thread, continuation and list file are held with no indication and no cancel. Dozens of long-lived children could starve the global queues the rest of the app uses. Category: leak.
fix: Keep the Process in a table and continue from terminationHandler; show waiting chains somewhere cancellable.

title: Application detection: a quoted app path with a space is cut inside the quotes.
detail: line.drop { $0 != " " } cuts inside the quotes. "/Applications/My App.app" %N becomes open -a "/Applications/My App.app" App.app" ..., a syntax error.

title: Application detection uses the GUI process PATH, not the login shell PATH, so typing docker or emacs opens a same-named .app.
detail: Typing docker or emacs with a same-named .app installed and the CLI in /opt/homebrew/bin opens the app.

title: A .app in the current folder wins over the command typed (Safari.app in a downloaded folder opens that one).
detail: Bare names never search "."; a file named ls does not shadow /bin/ls.

title: Command history with secrets is persisted and exported with default 0644 permissions.
detail: Every typed line (curl -u user:pass, mysql -p...) is stored in systemTools.history. Export includes every stored key and writes the file with default 0644.
fix: Offer "do not record" for history; exclude history from export or warn; write the export 0600.

title: Passwords are encoded into virtual folder URLs and land in tabs, history and hotlist.
detail: Comment says "scheme, user, host and port" but a password is included: ftp://user:s3cret@host becomes hex in the vfolder:// host (encoding confirmed). Same if a real URL carries a password: DirectoryHistory.swift:34 and TreeCache.swift:188 store absoluteString. Whether Network URLs ever carry one was not verified.
fix: Strip the password in prefix(of:) and before persisting.

title: Jobs that ignore cancellation can block the command system (Rename Volume, Eject, System Information on a stale mount).
detail: resourceValues on a dead network mount can hang; the job ignores its monitor and Kernel.swift:79 blocks commands while isBusy is true. Trigger with a stale NFS/SMB mount. Plausible, not reproduced. Category: freeze.
fix: Run these outside the job queue with a timeout, and abandon on cancel.

title: Branch view memory and re-walk storms.
detail: visited collects every directory URL (hundreds of MB for a large branch) yet only the first 512 are kept. Only those 512 directories are watched so deeper changes go unseen. Every change report triggers a full re-walk on all cores, at most every 0.5 s, for as long as changes continue; a branch of ~ or of a build folder would re-walk constantly unless the panel debounces (not verified). With no cancellation flag, receive is only consulted when a batch has files, so a directory-only region cannot be stopped. Coalescer can call onChange up to 0.5 s after the watcher was released. 64 remembered lists have no entry cap.
fix: Cap visited at watchLimit; for local branches use one recursive watch on the root; back off re-walks; check a weak token in settle.

title: List files are line-based with no escaping, so a name with a newline injects extra lines into %L/%F.
detail: A file named "x\n/Users/me/important" contributes two lines to %L/%F; xargs rm < %L then removes another path. %F names beginning with - are not protected.
fix: Refuse names with newlines (as missingName refuses), or offer a NUL-separated list code.

title: TreeCache: a stale file can be left after a flush/store race.
detail: flush snapshots an entry, store then writes a newer one, and flush writes the old snapshot last; file on disk is stale after restart.

title: TreeCache: subtrees silently lost because line.hasPrefix("[") is Character-based (folder name starting with a combining mark never parses back).
TreeCache: slow parse, line.count and text.contains are grapheme-based over files of 100 MB scale.
fix: Use utf8.

title: TreeCache: memory is never evicted; a million-folder tree is held as full path strings plus a Set plus the formatted text during write.
TreeCache: folders added by noteFolder load as scanned and show as leaves even if they have subfolders.

TreeCache threading is sound: the lock is never held during disk I/O and the main thread takes it only in flush() at quit; a hostile cache file can only produce odd names (..), leading to navigation, not a crash.
Real folders named like virtual ones (" (branch)", " (list N)", " (selected branch N)") are unreachable by typed path.
detail: Any text ending in these suffixes is claimed first: a real /x/Photos (branch), typed or stored in the hotlist as cd /x/Photos (branch), opens the branch view of /x/Photos. The (list N) form also ignores the title.

title: Tree attach: the merge path ignores limit, so a huge folder on the selected-folder ancestor chain links in one turn.
detail: Taken for every ancestor of the selected folder because those are pre-created.

title: Tree attach: a partial attach across turns can interleave with a node(at:creating:) insert and give duplicate or out-of-order children.
Dropping a million-node tree frees it on the main thread.
fix: Hand it to a background queue.

title: A cancelled non-rescan tree scan still stores its partial result after a newer scan began.
detail: Harmless ordering in practice.

title: Tree ownership is clean: nodes are built off-main and touched only on main afterwards, and generation checks cover every hop.
.unreadable settings backups are written only if none exists, never removed, and exported; a second corruption is not backed up and the next save drops the unreadable entries.
Start-menu slots: ensureSlots registers one command per entry with no cap; an imported million-entry menu stalls main. Hotlist.limit is likewise enforced on insert only.
An empty value produces no word (%E without extension, empty variable), shifting later arguments.
fix: Emit "".

title: Double escaping: "...%S..." re-escapes the user's own text ("$HOME/%S" becomes \$HOME) and the tail scan ignores \".
A very large selection in %S exceeds ARG_MAX; the error reads "cannot be started".
List cleanup timing: quit deletes list files that programs started in the last 60 s may still need; the start-time async delete can race the first list write.
Pid reuse only leaks a folder; the parent is the per-user temp directory so no symlink or predictable-name issue.
Hotlist "add current dir": a folder with a trailing space, or one named ":", is stored as cd <path> and trimmed or reinterpreted on use.
capabilities without a location answers for the folder read last, wrong with two different virtual panels.
Lists shown without any watcher (unwatchable provider, empty list, background tab) can be evicted while shown.
List file is read without a size cap; lines may name any provider so opening a list file causes connections.
PagePrintView.init counts graphemes of every line on main.
History bookkeeping does 200 URL parses on main per navigation.
Virtual URL decoding: decoded prefixes may carry a path or query and the path is not standardised (.../a/../../etc accepted).
detail: Navigation only.

title: Shared state: CommandRunner.active/launched/environment main only (race-free; active logically wrong, finding 8); list folder benign races; ConfigurationStore caches, ConfigurationCenter, key-binding editors main only; ProcessRunner.Buffer NSLock; SystemTools.log main only; DirectoryTree/TreeNode built on one thread handed to main; TreeScanner.paths/unscanned scan thread only; tree window state main only; TreeCache.memory under NSLock with no I/O under lock (stale-write race finding 15); DirectoryHistoryTracker main only; VirtualFileSystem state under one NSLock never held across a walk or provider call (register holds it O(n) on main, finding 5); Coalescer own NSLock (late callback, finding 13).
Cancelling a typed command: the child leads its own process group; after terminate no orphan remained for "a; b" or a pipeline in zsh, bash, sh, dash (confirmed in pg/).
Output handling: the 8 MB cap keeps draining, the parent write end is closed, and lpr gets absolute paths.
Open Terminal Here uses NSWorkspace.open with no AppleScript and no shell string, so no injection through directory names.

Ordinary hostile names in plain contexts (%N, "%N", '%N', %P%N, x%Ny, --out=%N) arrive as exactly one correct argument in zsh, bash, sh, dash, ksh for every name without a combining mark (spaces, quotes, backslash, $, backtick, ;&|<>, globs, ~, !, #, =, newline, CR, tab, U+2028, 250-byte name); the ./ prefix for - names works.
No-name refusal: missingName refuses %N, %O, %E, %V and %M on [..]; %P%S with nothing selected expands to nothing rather than the bare folder.
Directory names cannot trigger a hotlist command: stored entries always start with cd .

Virtual folder URLs round-trip for spaces, %, #, ?, ;, newline, combining marks, trailing space and very long hosts; lists are refused for every mutating call; move, copy, remove, trash, append, commit, setQuarantine and copyMetadata map source and destination consistently.
Options window, key-binding rebase, command browser modal, hotlist editor: no threading issues found.
fish, nu and other non-POSIX shells were not installed and not tested.
CommandLanguage.expandingEnvironment was not run; it shares the helpers from finding 1.
How the panel reacts to onChange bursts, and how the shell builds destination URLs for items shown under display-path names in picked views, were not reviewed.
Whether Network URLs ever carry passwords was not verified.
The form/list UI handling of newlines and very long titles was not reviewed.
JobService internals beyond the protocol comment were not reviewed.
Nothing was run inside the app: no build, and no TCC or File Provider behaviour observed live.
One deep path in an archive exhausts memory on Enter (quadratic ArchiveTree.insert).
detail: insert walks up the parents and each step allocates a new full-length parent string kept as a dictionary key and entry path; cost and retained memory are quadratic in path length. One ZIP entry with a 65,533-byte name a/a/a/... creates 32,768 implicit folders; in a replica of the tree key handling this retained 1.07 GB of key bytes (1.2 GB RSS) and took 4.9 s. Twenty such entries fit in a ~2.6 MB ZIP. A pax path record may be 16 MB (about 8 million components) so a .tar.gz of a few tens of KB never finishes, and the loop has no cancellation check. Security (DoS).
fix: Reject paths over about 4 KB or 256 components before inserting; store children as nodes rather than full-path keys; check the interrupt inside indexing.

title: Quit can silently drop changes to nested or remote archives (flushAll makes one pass).
detail: flushAll makes one pass over opened.values in dictionary order. Flushing an inner archive uploads into its outer archive, giving the outer new pending changes. If the outer was visited first nothing flushes it again, failures is empty, no rescue runs, and store.close() deletes the spools. Trigger: copy a file into outer.zip/inner.zip and quit within the idle delay (up to 60 s for the outer, since replacing the inner counts as a removal). Data loss.
fix: Repeat until no archive has pending changes (bounded passes), or flush deepest first; run the rescue for anything still pending.

title: A deletion made while a flush is building never reaches the disk.
detail: take counts a removal only if the record is already in the archive. A member that is still a spool when the snapshot is taken, then removed during the build, is written into the new file. install skips it because it is gone from the tree, and the next snapshot finds no work and marks everything written. Trigger: add files to a large ZIP, then delete one while the rewrite runs (minutes for big archives); the file stays in the archive on disk and reappears after a restart. A job .afm-<UUID>.tmp member discarded during a flush persists the same way. Correctness/privacy.
fix: In install, for every snapshot entry that was written but is no longer in the tree, increment removals.

title: Pack into a ZIP on a server or inside another archive deletes the old member on failure and ignores Encrypt.
detail: Data loss: the existing member is removed before the replacement is written; on a read error or Cancel the handler flushes, making the removal permanent with no replacement. Security: options.password and options.level are never used on this path; with Encrypt ticked members are stored in plain text and the verify pass succeeds because there is nothing to decrypt.
fix: Write under a temporary name and move(replacing: true) on success; refuse or implement encryption on this path.

title: Quit blocks the main thread on archive writes (flushAll on main, uncancellable).
detail: applicationWillTerminate calls kernel.shutdown() which calls stop() which runs flushAll() on the main thread: whole-archive rewrites and uploads with no progress and no cancellation (upload creates a flag nobody can set). Also waits on flushLock behind any timer flush in progress, as does rescue(). Trigger: quit while a multi-GB rewrite is pending, or with an unresponsive server. Possible hard deadlock (plausible, depends on remote provider): a background flush holding flushLock whose provider calls kernel.askUser (a main.sync) deadlocks against the main thread waiting in flushAll.
fix: Flush from applicationShouldTerminate via .terminateLater on a background thread with a progress window and cancellation flag; acquire flushLock with lock(before:).

title: capabilities(for:) on the main thread takes the archive lock, which is held across disk I/O and O(n log n) work.
detail: Same lock held during: isCurrent() stat (481-484); requireEditable() two access() calls or another provider capabilities (681-689); clones() clonefile + unlink (768-779); finishWrite statfs and possibly a volume resource query (842-850); takeSnapshot full sort and copy of all entries (1104-1138); install stat, open, rename and a walk over all entries (1267-1307); rebase re-reading and parsing the whole directory (1312-1352). Trigger: archive on a stalled SMB/NFS mount where a background stat holds the lock until the mount times out; or a 1M-entry ZIP during snapshot or rebase. Freeze.
fix: Keep capability inputs (editable, hasDuplicates, fetched) in a separate tiny lock or atomic updated at load/rebase; move all syscalls out of the directory lock.

title: bsdtar accepts an mtree text file and reads local files it names.
detail: Anything not recognised becomes .foreign and is passed to bsdtar -cf - @file; libarchive mtree reader opens contents= paths. A text file named holiday.7z containing #mtree and "photo.jpg type=file contents=/path/to/secret" lists photo.jpg with the secret file bytes, read with the app privileges. A large local file is copied into scratch (up to 4 GB); a FIFO hangs the child until cancelled. Security.
fix: Accept only known magic numbers for foreign formats (7z, Rar!, MSCF, xar!, cpio, ISO, LHA) before calling bsdtar; run with an empty working directory and minimal environment, ideally sandboxed to read only the archive.

title: Nothing is synced before the rename though commit promises durability.
detail: After a power loss the rename can be durable while the appended tail and new directory are not: a ZIP with no central directory, and Move or Move-to-archive has already deleted the sources. Plausible.
fix: fsync (or F_BARRIERFSYNC) the temporary file before rename, at least on commit and Move-to-archive paths.

title: Pack into an existing local ZIP bypasses OpenArchive: lost update and widened file mode.
detail: Lost update (plausible): appendToZip and writeZip read the directory at the start and rename at the end with no flushLock and no signature check; a flush or another program writing in between is overwritten. try? store.flush also ignores failure. Mode widened (confirmed by reading): the rewrite path creates the file 0644 and never applies the old mode, so a 0600 archive becomes world-readable.
fix: Go through the open archive under its flushLock, or re-check FileSignature before the rename; chmod as OpenArchive.build does.

title: ".." filter bypass via combining characters (Character-based splitting).
detail: Swift splits on Characters; / followed by a combining mark (U+0301, ZWJ, variation selectors) is a single Character not equal to /. The name ../\u{301}evil.txt normalises to itself and the unpack target becomes <folder>/../(combining)evil.txt. Limits: one level above the target and the file name must start with a combining mark. Reachable through Unpack; ordinary Copy fails to read such an item. Security.
fix: Split on bytes (utf8, 0x2F) everywhere (normalized, name(of:), parent(of:), the Unpacker); reject NUL and control characters; assert the final target isInside the folder.

title: No cap on entry count; about 0.5-1 KB of memory per entry.
detail: A .tgz of roughly 1 MB can hold a million empty members; larger ones tens of millions. Each entry carries an ArchiveEntry with an inline ZipRecord, three or four strings and a set element. Eviction is by count (12), not by memory. Per-entry figure is an estimate, not measured. Plausible.
fix: Cap entries (a few million) with a clear error; consider a compact entry representation.

title: Password prompt storm, and no serialisation of prompts.
detail: Every member whose check byte fails prompts up to three times. Parallel readers prompt concurrently. A refusal is not remembered. A ZIP with thousands of "encrypted" entries with differing check bytes makes Test or Unpack produce thousands of modal dialogs; only the job Cancel stops them. Related, low: Unpacker.run unlocks the whole archive even when the selection has no encrypted member.
fix: One prompt gate per archive (re-check the cache after acquiring it); remember "declined" for the duration of the operation.

title: Members under temporary names can be persisted and remain in the archive.
detail: Only the immediate write leaves out arriving members. The timer, another job commit, the store.flush calls of Unpack/Test/Pack, and flushAll at quit all write closed-but-unrenamed members under .afm-<UUID>.tmp. They remain if: the process exits or crashes before the rename; the job discards the temp member while a flush is building (finding 3); the writer landed in an orphaned OpenArchive (finding 24). Otherwise the later rename appends the data a second time and leaves dead space.
fix: Never include arriving members in a flush unless the caller asks; at quit drop them; at load optionally hide or strip names matching the temp pattern.

title: Spools go to TMPDIR on the boot volume with no space check there.
detail: finishWrite checks room only at the archive folder. On a file system that cannot clone (exFAT, HFS+, SMB) immediate writes never happen, so a whole job compressed data accumulates in TMPDIR. Copying 200 GB into a ZIP on a USB drive needs 200 GB free on the boot disk and fails with "no space" although the destination has room.
fix: Spool next to the archive when it is on another volume, or check scratch space and flush early.

title: Scratch disk exhaustion when entering stream archives or fetching remote/nested archives.
detail: Merely entering a stream archive of 256 MB or less writes up to 4 GB into scratch; twelve cached archives can hold 48 GB. No free-space check beforehand; a failed write is caught but the disk stays full until indexing ends. Fetching a remote or nested archive copies it whole with no size or space check; a nested member can declare any size.
fix: A budget for total scratch use, a "keep N GB free" check before and during materialisation, and a hasRoom check against item.size before fetching.

title: Cancellation gaps: archive opens, flushLock and isCurrent are not cancellable.
detail: store.archive(at:) is called without the job flag at those sites; a long open (bsdtar, bzip2, counting a .bz2 to its end) cannot be cancelled and waiters on the same slot block. flush() takes flushLock unconditionally (1045), so commit and the immediate write in move (937, no flag at all) wait behind a multi-minute timer rewrite. isCurrent() does an uncancellable remote item(at:) under the slot lock (491).
fix: Thread the flag through; use lock(before:) polling; use flushLock.try() for the opportunistic write in move.

title: Editing an archive reached through a symbolic link replaces the link.
detail: clonefile and stat follow the link but rename(temp, localURL.path) replaces the link itself with a new file; the real archive never changes. Plausible.
fix: Resolve the last path component once at open and use the real path.

title: Child processes re-open the archive by path, so a replaced file returns member N of the new file under the old name.
detail: For bzip2 and bsdtar, members are found by index in a stream started from file.path. If the file is replaced while a job still holds entries of the old OpenArchive, member N of the new file is returned with no error. Nothing compares the header path or size with the entry. Plausible.
fix: Give the child the already-open file (stdin; bsdtar ... @-) and verify header name and size on .member opens.

title: Random-order reads of big stream archives are quadratic.
detail: Only Unpacker uses readInOnePass. Ordinary Copy takes files in panel order. For a non-materialised archive (over 256 MB) that is uncorrelated with archive order, so each file decompresses a large fraction of the archive, with at most four parked readers. Plausible.
fix: Materialise lazily when a second restart happens and space allows, or expose archive order or a batch API to the job.

title: Listing a foreign archive means full extraction through a pipe.
detail: Every open of a 7z/rar/iso decompresses all data just to see the headers. Above 256 MB nothing is kept, so each member read (or parked-reader miss) runs bsdtar from the start again.
fix: Accept the trade-off knowingly, or list with libarchive directly.

title: Failed-flush retry rewrites the whole archive every 30 s forever.
detail: Deterministic failures (a damaged member copyMember rejects, an archive deleted or moved, a name too long) are retried at a fixed interval; each try may copy gigabytes to a temp file before failing.
fix: Exponential back-off; do not retry failures that cannot heal until the next change.

title: Deferred writes are invisible to the rest of the app (archive stale if moved/copied during the idle window).
detail: Deletions wait min(60, 20 x lastRewriteDuration) seconds. If the user moves, copies or uploads the archive file in another panel during that window the file is stale. A moved archive then fails with "changed by another program" forever, and the changes end up in a rescue ZIP at quit. Design data-loss risk, plausible.
fix: Let the kernel ask providers to commit before a file that is an open archive is read, moved or deleted; show pending state in the panel.

title: correctTime patches before verifying; canAppend checks only the header offset.
detail: The four DOS-time bytes are written at offset + 10 before the local signature is checked. With a crafted directory offset this overwrites another member data. A member whose data runs past directoryOffset is cut by the truncation. Security/correctness.
fix: Verify signature and name first; require offset + 30 + name + extra + compressedSize <= directoryOffset.

title: A writer can land in an archive the store has just dropped.
detail: Between store.archive() returning and archive.write(), eviction or the not-current replacement can remove the archive from the table. Later rename and commit go to a new instance: the job fails loudly but the orphan flushes its temp-named member by itself. store.commit also returns success when no archive is in the table. Threading, plausible (narrow window).
fix: A "detached" flag set under the archive lock that makes write throw or retry; register the writer under the slot lock.

title: Leftovers after a crash and loose scratch permissions.
detail: .UUID.afm-zip.tmp and .afm-pack.tmp files (full size on the rewrite path) and scratch folders are never swept. Scratch directory is created 0755 with files 0644, which matters only if TMPDIR is shared.
fix: Sweep at start (the pid is in the scratch name); create the directory 0700 and files 0600.

title: Cached open failures never expire for local files.
detail: A transient error (ENOSPC in scratch, a killed child) is replayed until the archive signature changes or the slot is evicted.
fix: Cache only format errors, with a time limit.

title: Each immediate write re-sorts and copies all entries.
detail: Any insert or remove clears orderedPaths so each immediate write costs O(n log n) under the lock.
fix: Keep the order incrementally (append when the order is the maximum).

title: Unpack follows symbolic links that already exist at the destination.
detail: A link created by an earlier extraction is followed by a later one. Within one run the order is safe. Security, plausible.
fix: lstat each created component; refuse to pass through links the run did not create.

title: Rollback in move can re-insert an entry with a stale order after a rebase.
detail: After a rebase inside the failed flush the restored replaced entry carries an order from the old tree, which can collide in built.offsets. Plausible (rare).
fix: Insert without keepingOrder when the tree was reloaded.

title: readInOnePass ends silently when the stream has fewer members than wanted.
fix: Throw if left > 0.

title: ZIP64 end record is not found behind a self-extractor stub.
detail: end64Offset is used unshifted so the reader falls back to the 32-bit fields. Plausible; not tested with a real ZIP64 SFX.

title: A valid .xz with long stream padding is reported damaged.
detail: Confirmed with a replica of the loop: padding of 64 KB and of 200 KB both fail.
fix: Skip zero bytes in a loop until non-zero or EOF.

title: install takes the new signature by stat on the path after the rename.
fix: Use fstat on newFile.

title: stop() keys rescue outcomes by file name, so two archives with the same name report the wrong path.
A hard-link entry whose path is later reused by a file overwrites that file content mapping.
After a failed upload remoteStamp may become nil and remote changes are then never detected.
The flush timer runs at .utility QoS; a user-initiated commit waiting behind it gets a CPU override but not its I/O tier.
ArchiveURL.make hex-encodes the outer authority so the host doubles per nesting level, and there is no nesting limit.
bsdtar and bzip2 inherit the full environment (bzip2 reads BZIP2/BZIP; libarchive may exec filter helpers found via PATH) and are not sandboxed.
Spools kept by rescue() are raw deflate streams with UUID names and no index.
Premise check: the archive lock is a plain NSLock, not recursive, and no nested acquisition was found.
Premise check: FindFiles cannot descend into nested archives because location(from:) only resolves local-disk archives; a quine archive is only reachable by entering it by hand.

Shared state is correctly guarded: OpenArchive state under lock (held too long, finding 6); archive file writes/upload/rescue under flushLock always taken before lock (not cancellable, Packer bypasses); format/archiveURL/quarantine/fetchedCopy immutable; ArchiveStore table lock is a leaf; Slot lock with try-based eviction (write-start race, finding 24); ArchiveEnvironment.options own lock, other fields set once by convention; StreamInterrupt/InterruptSlot own locks and handlers run outside; ProcessStream errors/isClosed own lock; ScratchFolder/TemporaryFile locks; ZipMemberWriter, ZipPacker, ParallelCompressor, OutputFile, TarReader and streams single owner thread; Unpacker/Packer counters on job thread with SharedCounter.

Lock order: slot -> table; slot -> archive; flushLock -> archive; inner archive -> table -> outer archive (via requireEditable); inner flushLock -> outer archive and outer flushLock (via upload). No inversion found. No holder of an archive lock calls the UI; askPassword is called with no archive lock held, possibly under the inner slot lock, which is safe because main never waits on a slot lock.

Parsers: no trap in 460,000 mutated ZIP, ZIP64, encrypted ZIP, pax/GNU tar, .tgz and .txz inputs; fuzzer covered directory, local header, extra fields, decrypt/inflate/size-guard/CRC, tar reader, pax records, xz index, gzip trailer and format detection; arithmetic clamped or range-checked.
bsdtar output is read as a TAR stream not text so names with newlines cannot spoof entries; tools invoked by absolute path with no shell; bzip2 gets --, bsdtar gets @ plus an absolute path.
Terminated children are reaped (20 terminated bsdtar, none left); the only pipe the app writes to has F_SETNOSIGPIPE.
Truncated xz, or xz with trailing garbage, ends with an error with no spin.

Flush atomicity: archive file is always the complete old or complete new one apart from durability (finding 8); disk full mid-append removes the clone; external change detected before build and again under the lock before rename; two flushes cannot overlap.
Readers during a flush stay consistent: readers hold records bound to their file object, listers see the tree only under the lock.
Timer: pending changes always imply an armed timer or running flush; no lost wake-up.
ZIP64 thresholds for count, offsets and sizes are handled on write and re-read; data descriptors rewritten correctly on copy; stub prefixes kept.
Read-only cases: duplicate-name archives are read-only on every mutating path; AES entries give a clear "not supported" error.
The cached password is dropped on a wrong check byte or CRC failure.
Parked readers are taken and returned under the lock; an interrupted reader is never parked.
Abandoned or cancelled opens cache nothing and their scratch files and children are removed.

Extraction order: within one Unpack run folders are created before any link and files arrive by temp + exclusive rename; a link entry followed by a file below it, or a case collision, cannot write through a link.
Ordinary Copy never creates links from archive members.
Setuid/setgid bits are masked for ZIP and TAR; device and FIFO entries are skipped (tar) or written as regular files (ZIP).
Quarantine is propagated to unpacked files and explicit folders.
NUL in names is not truncated by URL.path; it stays %00.
The project was not built and its test suite was not run; findings marked confirmed by reading were not reproduced at runtime.
Not exercised: crash and power-loss behaviour, non-APFS volumes, SMB stalls.
Outside scope: Tests/, and FileJob beyond its transfer, temp-name and commit paths.
Outside scope: the network providers, including whether one can call askUser during an upload (which decides the deadlock in finding 5).
Main-thread callers in the shell were checked only by grep.
Not measured: Apple LZMA decoder with a multi-GB declared dictionary.
libarchive own parsers inside bsdtar are untrusted-input code that was not examined.
The cost-limited Myers split produces grossly wrong diffs on large files.
detail: When a split hits limit (256 for typical sizes) only the furthest point of the forward walk is used. If files are shifted by more than limit lines that also occur on the other side, each split lands on a random diagonal and the rest of the file is consumed as "different". Trigger: files of 20,000+ lines after filtering with a large moved or deleted block plus scattered edits. Seeded runs, 20/20 seeds each: 30k-line source-like file, 300 edits, 2,000-line block deleted: 25,894 changed lines shown, shortest script 2,548; 400-line block moved plus 100 edits: 46,806 shown, shortest 994; 500 edits plus a 500-line block deleted (random values): 47,224 shown, shortest 1,458 (17/20 seeds). The script is always valid but shows nearly identical files as almost entirely different.
fix: At the limit choose the split from whichever walk progressed further, or the diagonal with the longest recent snake as GNU diff does. Better, anchor on lines unique to both sides (patience/histogram) before falling back to Myers.

title: SFV entries whose name starts with ; or # are never verified.
detail: Create writes "#notes.txt 1A2B3C4D"; Verify treats the line as a comment. An .sfv for #notes.txt, ;x.txt, ok.txt with the first two damaged verified as "CRC32: Errors: 0", one row.
fix: Do not treat # as a comment in SFV; write ./name for names starting with ;; or refuse such names in the SFV format.

title: Unreadable checksum lines and empty checksum files report "Errors: 0".
detail: A line with a damaged digest (one hex digit short), an empty file, or a file of junk each yield zero rows and "Checksums: Errors: 0" (short.sha256, empty.md5, junk.md5 all gave zero rows and no error). Related, low, confirmed by reading: run.contents(of:) silently stops at 64 MiB (ToolRun.swift:150), so entries beyond it are never verified.
fix: Count non-comment lines that do not parse as errors ("cannot read line N") and treat a checksum file with no entries as a failure.

title: URL-safe Base64 decode is cut at "--" (taken for a MIME boundary) and reports success with a truncated file.
detail: The alphabet accepts - and _, but a line or 64 K piece starting with -- is taken for a MIME boundary. A file starting "----" decoded to 0 bytes; a one-line file whose second 64 K piece starts with -- decoded to 49,152 of 98,604 bytes. For random data about 1 in 4,096 per piece.
fix: Only treat -- as a boundary when the body came from MIME headers.

title: Decode appends unrelated numbered sibling files (photo1.b64 + photo2.b64) into one output.
detail: photo1.b64 and photo2.b64, both plain base64 output without padding, decoded to one 6,000-byte file (photo1 + photo2). A crafted file can pull numbered siblings into the output the same way.
