fix: Only continue into further parts for bodies that began with a header, or when the first part ends on a full line.

title: Damaged UUE/XXE lines are dropped silently (855 of 900 bytes written, no error); the sum -r/size trailer is never checked.
fix: Report "incomplete or damaged" and keep or flag the output.

title: A missing "end" in UUE/XXE is accepted: a multi-part set with a missing last part yields a short file and success.
fix: Report "incomplete or damaged" and keep or flag the output.

title: yEnc size= and crc32= are never checked: a truncated body with a wrong CRC decoded to 9 of 16 bytes with no error.
fix: Report "incomplete or damaged" and keep or flag the output.

title: Unsaved Compare edits are lost on quit.
detail: stop() calls close(), which bypasses windowShouldClose. Shell.swift:103 only asks the job service, so Cmd+Q with edited files discards them silently. Data loss.
fix: Have the plugin veto or prompt on termination.

title: Save fallback can delete both the original and the new content.
detail: If move(replacing: true) fails the code does remove(url) then move(temporary, to: url); if that second move fails the outer catch removes the temporary as well. Trigger: a provider that cannot rename over an existing file (typical SFTP/FTP) plus a dropped connection or error between the two steps. Plausible.
fix: Move the original aside as SyncExecutor does, and never delete the temporary once the original is gone.

title: Private files are world-readable while being saved or copied.
detail: Local write opens with 0o644; permissions are applied only in close(attributes:). Saving a 0600 file writes its full content to .name.afm-save readable by others first. Same for streamed sync copies. Security.
fix: Create with 0600 and widen at close.

title: clear() resets the sync phase while a comparison or sync job is running.
detail: adopt() (command is runsDuringJobs: true) and loadSet() (the star menu is always live) call clear(), which sets phase = .idle without cancelling running. During a sync job Compare and Synchronize become available again, a comparison runs over trees being modified, and a second plan is queued. During a comparison the old one keeps running uncancelled; if the user does not start a new one its rows are installed under the newly shown paths; the Synchronize dialog delete lines name no directory.
fix: Refuse adopt/loadSet while synchronizing; in clear() cancel and nil running.

title: Mirror mode has no guard against an empty or unmounted left side.
detail: A root that fails to list is handled correctly (no rows, error shown). A root that lists as empty (leftover mount point, empty share) makes every right file .rightOnly, proposed as deleteRight with the box pre-checked. Deletion is direct where there is no Trash. Data loss.
fix: When one root is empty and the other is not in asymmetric mode, ask explicitly, name the directory in the delete line, and default the box off.

title: Sync outcome is never shown; commit failures are silent.
detail: outcome.errors, skipped and wasCancelled are never read. A failed commit on a deferred-write destination stops the deletions but tells the user nothing; the result of the final commitWrites() is discarded.
fix: Show a summary when there were errors or a commit failed.

title: Cancel during a sync copy leaves a stray temporary.
detail: When the same-volume copy to the temporary completes and the flag is set, transfer throws Cancelled outside the do that removes the temporary. Result: [".f.bin.afm-sync", "f.bin"] left in the target.
fix: Wrap transfer in the cleanup.

title: A listing cut short by cancel is trusted as an empty folder, so a non-empty folder may be removed or trashed.
detail: The local list returns [] without throwing once the flag is set. perform(deletion) then went on to remove a non-empty folder; only rmdir refusing saved it ("Directory not empty"). With Trash on, trashItem would move the whole folder including files the user chose to keep. removeEmptyDirectories has the same pattern. Window is narrow (cancel between the step check and the first listing buffer).
fix: Re-check the flag after every list before acting on the result.

title: Case-colliding names are paired as "left only", risking replacement of a file on a case-insensitive side.
detail: Left {a.txt, A.txt} against right {a.txt} gives A.txt <-> - as .leftOnly. Copying to a case-insensitive right replaces a.txt; the next sync flips back. With three names folding alike, two become one-sided. With Confirm overwrites off or after "Overwrite All" it is silent. Data loss.
fix: Mark a leftover as excluded when its folded name equals a name already used on the other side.

title: Cleanup after Overwrite + cancel deletes files that were there before; same-location guards miss case variants, symlinked dirs and hard links.
detail: written holds final URLs, so on failure the cleanup removes the old file that the temp-then-rename scheme deliberately kept. Split into a folder holding old data.001/data.002, Overwrite all, cancel: folder ends with only old data.002 (test for finished parts; reading for the in-progress part). The "output equals source" guards use isSameLocation, a plain string compare; they miss case variants (X.CRC vs X.crc), symlinked directories (/tmp vs /private/tmp) and hard links. Combined with the cleanup the source can be deleted after an Overwrite confirmation. Data loss.
fix: Track which outputs replaced existing files and only remove what the run created; compare by device/inode for local files.

title: A cancelled Compare can leave a stale diff in phase .ready, so copy(rows:) traps or copies wrong lines.
detail: Trigger: edit a file of 20,000+ lines (content becomes new documents plus old diff, background recompute starts), press Compare (supersedes the recompute), press Esc. "What was shown before stays" leaves new documents with old row indexes. copy(rows:) then indexes source.lines[$0] and target.lines[range] unchecked: it traps, or copies the wrong lines, which can then be saved. Plausible.
fix: Re-run recompute() when a compare is cancelled over edited content, or block editing until the diff is current.

title: Main-thread stall: within-line highlight costs about 77 ms per changed row for long differing lines.
detail: About 77 ms per changed row for two 4,096-unit lines with little in common. A screenful of long differing lines (minified JSON, base64) is seconds on first draw and stutter while scrolling. Measured, release build.
fix: Compute off-thread and reload the row, or cap the effort.

title: Main-thread stall: inline recompute under 20,000 lines runs synchronously on every edit and option toggle.
detail: 2 x 9,999 lines with repeated lines took 210-620 ms. Measured, release build.
fix: Lower the threshold to about 2,000 lines or always go to the background.

title: Main-thread stall: sync list rebuild/plan/sort at 1M rows.
detail: rebuild() about 385 ms per Show toggle at 1M rows, plan() about 380 ms, sorting 1M rows of one folder by size or date 3.7 s. Measured, release build.
fix: Sort on extracted keys, off the main thread for large lists.

title: The sync executor ignores timeOffsetHours.
detail: adjustDate sets the target to the source date (or the source to the target date) with no offset, while classify adds the offset. With dT != 0 every copied pair shows as different again at the next compare.

title: Encode traps on a huge "Lines per file" (limit * method.lineLength overflows, e.g. 999999999999999999) and kills the app.
Encode reuses the last part name if the source grew since the panel listed it; the user is asked to overwrite the tool own earlier part.
Names with a line feed produce a checksum file that fails its own verify (notFound); no GNU escaping on write, and the same gap lets a file name inject extra lines.

Compare save is lossy and unchecked: allowLossyConversion turns characters outside Latin-1 into ?; invalid sequences in a BOM-marked file are rewritten as U+FFFD; no check that the file changed on disk since loading; hard links broken by the rename; a file compared with itself is written twice.
Close after "Save" can drop newer edits: completion(true) fires even when an edit arrived during the job.
Stale Find results: findGeneration is not bumped by recompute, swap, resync or compare, so a result can jump to a row of the old diff (bounds-checked, harmless).
Sort order differs from the system for digit runs above 2^64: localizedStandardCompare wraps; the fast path compares correctly.
detail: One disagreement in 1.2M fuzzed pairs. Display order only; nothing searches the order.

title: A cancelled sync comparison is not labelled: rows are valid but partial and Synchronize is enabled.
.name.afm-old is deleted at the start of the next attempt even when a failed restore left it as the only copy of the old file.
Streamed (cross-provider) file copies never call copyMetadata.
BLAKE3 uses the cores poorly on 1 MiB blocks: 706 MB/s against 338 MB/s serial on 16 cores; concurrentPerform fires for subtrees as small as 16 chunks.
fix: Larger read blocks for BLAKE3 would help.

title: Pause stops only one hashing thread: the thread holding reportLock blocks in the gate, the others skip via try().
Undo memory: up to 20 snapshots, each edit copying the edited side line array (about 64 MB at 2M lines).
Within-line ranges can split a surrogate pair or isolate a combining mark (41..<42 in both tests); guarded by upperBound <= length; cosmetic.
Hashes.swift needs the macOS 26 SDK to compile (SHA3_256 under #available).

Shared state: ToolRun counters/lines/lastReport under lock with reports serialised by reportLock; ToolRun.overwritesAll, ToolOutput, FolderSink, DecodeMachine job thread only; hasher instances one thread per block; BLAKE3 values buffer disjoint slots; SyncComparison counters/errors NSLock; lastReport in SyncSession.compare only in serialised calls; SyncExecutor fields job thread; CompareLoader.identical NSLock; FileTools.createChecksums written on job thread read in completion. SyncSession and CompareSession are main-thread with stale guards (running === ..., findGeneration, editGeneration) and are NOT sufficient: see findings 8 and 15.

BLAKE3: all 35 official vectors pass, one-shot and streamed, including lengths 3-8 and 127-129; streaming at 1 byte, fixed steps and 50 random chunkings; inputs up to 16 MiB + 1024 identical across parallel, 1 MiB-block and random-chunk paths versus serial.

SHA-3 224/256/384/512 match Python hashlib (empty, abc, 1 MB pattern, rate-boundary lengths); CryptoKit path and Swift fallback agree incl. random chunking; SHA3-224 1 MB matches openssl; rotation counts all 1-62.
CRC32, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2 match hashlib/zlib (225 digests, 0 bad); Data slices with a non-zero start index handled.
Myers: 400,000 fuzzed cases with limits nil/0/1/2/3/5/8/100 always gave a valid script, shortest when unlimited; debug build with bounds checks never trapped; empty against non-empty is correct.
TextDiff: 32,000 fuzzed cases with anchors, all option combinations and non-ASCII were valid; equal keys always hash equal and every .equal row is re-checked with isSameKey.

Verify logic: no path turns a mismatch into OK; empty digests of uncomputed methods cannot match; cancel throws; unreadable files give readError; result ordering preserved; absolute and ../ names are only read.
Decoders: 300,000 random UUE/XXE lines without a trap; header names cannot leave the target; header modes are ignored (4755 became 644).

Sync: symlinks never followed or deleted; a failed or cancelled listing of either side drops the folder on both; content read errors give .pending with no action; deletions run after commit, files before folders; canSynchronize and the plan cannot diverge.
Save: symlinks are resolved and the temporary is created with O_EXCL.
BLAKE3 beyond 4 GiB / 2^32 chunks not checked: counter is 64-bit by reading, no reference tool available.
Remote and archive providers behaviour under findings 6, 10 and 12 not reviewed.
AppKit windows were read, not driven: 8M-row tables, sheet/progress interplay and the 1M-row UI measured only at model level.
A real macOS < 26 system not tested: the fallback class was exercised directly on macOS 27.
Unpacker.run unlocks the whole archive even when the selection has no encrypted member.
detail: Related to the password prompt storm (finding 12).

title: run.contents(of:) silently stops at 64 MiB, so checksum entries beyond it are never verified.
detail: Related to finding 3.

title: The "output equals source" guards use isSameLocation, a plain string compare, missing case variants (X.CRC vs X.crc), symlinked directories (/tmp vs /private/tmp) and hard links; with the Overwrite cleanup the source can be deleted.
detail: Part of finding 14.
fix: Compare by device/inode for local files.
